questions.q: What must be configured on the logical server before any CREATE USER ... FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER statement can succeed in a database?
options: A Microsoft Entra admin must be set on the logical server first
The database must first be converted to SQL authentication
Nothing — Entra users can be created with no prior server configuration
A firewall rule allowing all IP addresses
questions.explain: Azure SQL needs at least one trusted Entra admin identity set at the server level before it can validate any other Entra identity against that tenant.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend setting the Entra admin to a group rather than one named person?
options: Admin membership can then change in Entra ID (someone joining or leaving the group) without ever touching SQL Server configuration
Groups are the only object type Azure SQL accepts as an admin
It makes the admin's password harder to guess
It automatically grants db_owner to everyone in the group
questions.explain: Using a group decouples who has admin rights from SQL Server configuration — membership changes happen entirely inside Entra ID.

questions.q: What is notably absent from creating an Entra-backed database user, compared to setting up a SQL-authenticated one?
options: A separate CREATE LOGIN step — the external identity itself is the credential
The database name
A username entirely
Any kind of permission model
questions.explain: CREATE USER ... FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER references the external Entra identity directly and serves as both the reference and the database-level object in one step, unlike SQL auth's separate CREATE LOGIN + CREATE USER pattern.

questions.q: Why does granting permissions to an Entra group scale better than granting them to individual users one at a time?
options: Every future member who joins that group in Entra ID automatically inherits the exact same access, with no repeated CREATE USER/GRANT pairs
Groups grant unlimited permissions automatically regardless of what's specified
Individual grants are not supported by Azure SQL at all
Group-based grants expire automatically after 90 days
questions.explain: A single GRANT to the group covers every current and future member, avoiding repeated setup and permission drift between team members over time.

questions.q: What is the correct order of steps for configuring Entra authentication on Azure SQL, per this lesson?
options: Set the Entra admin on the server, connect as that admin, CREATE USER FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER inside the database, then assign roles/grants
GRANT permissions first, then create the user, then set the server admin last
CREATE USER can happen before the server admin is ever set
The order does not matter at all
questions.explain: Skipping the server-level admin step and jumping straight to CREATE USER fails outright — the steps have a required dependency order.
